newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan May export orders up 4.2 percent yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan May export orders up 4.2 percent yr/yr.

text.p: Foreign orders for Taiwan goods rose 4.2 percent to US$10.45 billion in May compared to May 1996, the economics ministry said in a surprise day-early announcement on Friday.

The closely watched indicator, issued a day early in what a ministry official said was a slip-up, was somewhat below an average 5.082 percent year-on-year forecast compiled from a June 19 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.
In month-to-month terms, the May figure came in below a 5.91 percent year-on-year rise in export orders reported for April.
A more detailed breakdown of foreign orders by region and category was expected to be issued at 0230 GMT on Saturday.

In the Reuters Poll, economists said they expected higher export order growth from Europe and the United States and that the Taiwan dollar's gradual depreciation against the U.S. dollar and the Japanese yen in recent weeks would have boosted Taiwan exporters' competitiveness worldwide.
The Taiwan dollar long hovered around T$27.5 to the U.S. dollar, but has slipped slowly in 1997 to below T$27.9. It closed on Friday at T$27.913.
Economists said they expected the local dollar's fall to show an effect on exports in the third quarter.

Economists said orders growth would continue to be offset in part by the loss of US$130 million a month in foreign orders for pork since late March following an islandwide outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease on Taiwan's hog farms.
